source: The clusters also show a broad range of sizes that can be fit well to an exponential distribution (Figure 2C), similar to that observed for stochastically assembled chemotaxis receptors in bacteria (Greenfield et al., 2009).

evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3A,B.

claim: The larger cluster size and area coverage at higher p-Nephrin density is most likely due to the larger degree of coalescence at higher cluster densities.
source: At a given time after Nck/N-WASP addition, higher density produces a larger average cluster size and correspondingly a larger fraction of total area covered by the clusters (Figure 3—figure supplement 3A,B, respectively), most likely due to the larger degree of coalescence at higher cluster densities.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3A,B.

claim: Within the p-Nephrin/Nck/N-WASP clusters, each of the proteins recovers nearly fully in tens to hundreds of seconds in FRAP experiments.
source: Within the clusters, each of the proteins recovers nearly fully in tens to hundreds of seconds (Figure 3B).
evidence: Supported by FRAP data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Even though the p-Nephrin/Nck/N-WASP clusters themselves are persistent for hours, the individual components exchange with the surroundings on time-scales of seconds to minutes.
source: Thus, even though the clusters themselves are persistent for hours, the individual components exchange with the surroundings on time-scales of seconds to minutes.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the FRAP data.

claim: The recovery profiles of p-Nephrin, Nck, and N-WASP in clusters can all be fit to a double-exponential but do not fit to a single-exponential.
source: The recovery profiles can all be fit to a double-exponential but do not fit to a single-exponential (see 'Materials and methods' for F-test statistics).
evidence: This is a statement about the fitting of FRAP data, with reference to statistical tests in Materials and methods.

claim: N-WASP in p-Nephrin/Nck/N-WASP clusters shows recovery time constants of τ-fast = 2.6 s (37%) and τ-slow = 43 s (63%).
source: N-WASP shows recovery time constants of τ-fast = 2.6 s (37%) and τ-slow = 43 s (63%).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from FRAP experiments.

claim: Nck in p-Nephrin/Nck/N-WASP clusters recovers with τ-fast = 1.6 s (49%) and τ-slow = 72 s (51%).
source: Nck recovers with τ-fast = 1.6 s (49%) and τ-slow = 72 s (51%).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from FRAP experiments.

claim: p-Nephrin in clusters recovers with τ-fast = 86 s (76%) and τ-slow = 526 s (24%).
source: p-Nephrin recovers with τ-fast = 86 s (76%) and τ-slow = 526 s (24%).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from FRAP experiments.

claim: In the non-clustered regions, p-nephrin recovery can be fit well to a single-exponential, with τ = 31 s.
source: In the non-clustered regions, p-nephrin recovery can be fit well to a single-exponential, with τ = 31 s, similar to the fast phase in the clusters but appreciably slower than recovery in the absence of Nck/N-WASP, where τ = 1.3 s (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from FRAP experiments, with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The dissociation of p-nephrin from the membrane occurs much more slowly (τ = 2080 s) than the FRAP recovery rates.
source: In independent experiments we found that the dissociation of p-nephrin from the membrane occurs much more slowly than these rates (τ = 2080 s, Figure 2—figure supplement 1D), indicating that the FRAP recovery of the protein is largely due to two-dimensional diffusion within the bilayer.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from dissociation experiments, with reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The FRAP recovery of p-nephrin is largely due to two-dimensional diffusion within the bilayer.
source: In independent experiments we found that the dissociation of p-nephrin from the membrane occurs much more slowly than these rates (τ = 2080 s, Figure 2—figure supplement 1D), indicating that the FRAP recovery of the protein is largely due to two-dimensional diffusion within the bilayer.
evidence: This is an inference from the comparison of FRAP recovery rates and dissociation rates.

claim: Nck and N-WASP likely recover through a combination of diffusion in the plane of the bilayer as well as binding and dissociation from the membrane.
source: By contrast, Nck and N-WASP likely recover through a combination of diffusion in the plane of the bilayer as well as binding and dissociation from the membrane.
evidence: This is an inference about the mechanism of FRAP recovery for Nck and N-WASP.

claim: Both the clustered regions and non-clustered regions of p-Nephrin contain small assemblies that slow p-nephrin dynamics relative to its free diffusion in the bilayer.
source: Nevertheless, the data suggest that both the clustered regions and non-clustered regions contain small assemblies that slow p-nephrin dynamics relative to its free diffusion in the bilayer.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the FRAP data.

claim: The clustered region of p-Nephrin likely contains additional assemblies that are larger and have greater degrees of crosslinking that appreciably slow dynamics further.
source: The clustered region likely contains additional assemblies that are larger and have greater degrees of crosslinking that appreciably slow dynamics further.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the FRAP data.

claim: Upon recruitment of Nck and N-WASP, membrane-bound p-nephrin undergoes a sharp thermodynamically controlled phase transition to produce dense dynamic puncta on the membrane.
source: Together, our data show that upon recruitment of Nck and N-WASP, membrane-bound p-nephrin undergoes a sharp thermodynamically controlled phase transition to produce dense dynamic puncta on the membrane.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the data presented.

claim: The three nephrin pTyr sites have essentially identical affinities for the Nck SH2 domain.
source: Previous studies showed that the three nephrin pTyr sites have essentially identical affinities for the Nck SH2 domain (Blasutig et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citation to Blasutig et al., 2008.

claim: At a membrane density of 1000 molecules/μm2 and in the presence of 500 nM N-WASP, p-Nephrin begins to show clusters at 200–300 nM Nck.
source: At a membrane density of 1000 molecules/μm2 and in the presence of 500 nM N-WASP, p-Nephrin begins to show clusters at 200–300 nM Nck.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the experiments.

claim: Under the same conditions as p-Nephrin, Nephrin2pY and Nephrin1pY do not cluster even at Nck concentrations greater than 10 µM.
source: Under the same conditions, Nephrin2pY and Nephrin1pY do not cluster even at Nck concentrations greater than 10 µM (Figure 4A) nor with their own densities increased to 3000 molecules/μm2.
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: If the concentrations of N-WASP and Nck are increased to 2 µM and 5 µM, respectively, Nephrin2pY produces clusters.
source: If the concentrations of N-WASP and Nck are increased to 2 µM and 5 µM, respectively, Nephrin2pY produces clusters (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Even at 5 µM N-WASP and 10 µM Nck, Nephrin1pY does not cluster.
source: However, even at 5 µM N-WASP and 10 µM Nck, Nephrin1pY does not cluster (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The valency of nephrin phosphorylation can control the critical concentration for puncta formation.
source: Thus, the valency of nephrin phosphorylation can control the critical concentration for puncta formation, as in the three-dimensional phase separation of this system (Li et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a conclusion from the valency experiments, with reference to previous work (Li et al., 2012).

claim: At 500 nM N-WASP, the trivalent Nck analog (SH3)3 induces clustering at 200 nM (SH3 module concentration).
source: At 500 nM N-WASP, the trivalent molecule (SH3)3 induces clustering at 200 nM (SH3 module concentration), whereas the di-valent (SH3)2 and monovalent (SH3)1 molecules do not cluster even at concentrations above 10 µM of the SH3 module concentrations (Figure 4B).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: At 500 nM N-WASP, the di-valent (SH3)2 and monovalent (SH3)1 Nck analogs do not cluster even at concentrations above 10 µM of the SH3 module concentrations.
source: At 500 nM N-WASP, the trivalent molecule (SH3)3 induces clustering at 200 nM (SH3 module concentration), whereas the di-valent (SH3)2 and monovalent (SH3)1 molecules do not cluster even at concentrations above 10 µM of the SH3 module concentrations (Figure 4B).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Increasing N-WASP concentration to 5 µM and (SH3)2 concentration to 5 µM (SH3 module concentration) produces clusters.
source: Increasing N-WASP concentration to 5 µM and (SH3)2 concentration to 5 µM (SH3 module concentration) produced clusters, whereas clusters were absent even with 5 µM N-WASP and 5 µM (SH3)1 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Clusters are absent even with 5 µM N-WASP and 5 µM (SH3)1.
source: Increasing N-WASP concentration to 5 µM and (SH3)2 concentration to 5 µM (SH3 module concentration) produced clusters, whereas clusters were absent even with 5 µM N-WASP and 5 µM (SH3)1 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The valency experiments demonstrate the strong dependence of clustering on valency of the interacting species.
source: These data demonstrate the strong dependence of clustering on valency of the interacting species.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the valency experiments.

claim: The binding affinity of the p-Nephrin motif to the SH2 domain of Nck is 370 nM.
source: The binding affinity of the p-Nephrin motif to the SH2 domain of Nck is 370 nM, as determined by isothermal titration calorimetry (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by ITC data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The binding affinity of the p-TIR motif to the SH2 domain of Nck is 40 nM.
source: For the p-TIR motif the affinity to the SH2 domain is 40 nM.
evidence: This is stated in the text, with ITC data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: In the presence of p-TIR, at a density of 2000 molecules/μm2, the clustering concentration of the trivalent SH3 protein, (SH3)3, is 100 nM.
source: In the presence of p-TIR, at a density of 2000 molecules/μm2, the clustering concentration of the trivalent SH3 protein, (SH3)3, is 100 nM, as opposed to 200 nM for p-Nephrin (Figure 5A).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The higher affinity interaction between p-TIR and Nck slows the recovery of Nck in FRAP experiments.
source: The higher affinity interaction also slows the recovery of Nck, as FRAP data demonstrate (Figure 5B).
evidence: Supported by FRAP data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Nck shows recovery rate constants of τ-fast = 6.5 s (46%) and τ-slow = 89.5 s (54%) when the clusters of p-TIR/Nck/N-WASP were photobleached.
source: Fitting to a double-exponential, Nck shows recovery rate constants of τ-fast = 6.5 s (46%) and τ-slow = 89.5 s (54%) when the clusters of p-TIR/Nck/N-WASP were photobleached.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from FRAP experiments.

claim: Nck shows recovery rates of τ-fast = 1.6 s (49%) and τ-slow = 73.2 s (51%) when the clusters of p-Nephrin/Nck/N-WASP were photobleached.
source: However, Nck shows recovery rates of τ-fast = 1.6 s (49%) and τ-slow = 73.2 s (51%) when the clusters of p-Nephrin/Nck/N-WASP were photobleached.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from FRAP experiments.

claim: Both the clustering concentrations and the dynamics of the clusters can be affected by molecular affinities.
source: Together, the data show that both the clustering concentrations and the dynamics of the clusters can be affected by molecular affinities, as expected of a crosslinked polymer network.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the affinity experiments.

claim: When a higher-affinity monovalent pTyr peptide is added in solution, the p-Nephrin/Nck/N-WASP clusters dissipate.
source: Additionally when a higher-affinity monovalent pTyr peptide is added in solution, the clusters dissipate.
evidence: This is an observation from the experiments.

claim: The clusters of p-Nephrin/Nck/N-WASP disappear within minutes after the addition of 10 μM monovalent TIR peptide.
source: In the presence of clusters made from 1 μM (SH3)3, 500 nM N-WASP and p-nephrin, we added singly phosphorylated TIR peptide (without a His tag) at 10 μM concentration (Video 3, Figure 6A). The clusters disappear within minutes after the addition of the monovalent peptide.
evidence: Supported by data shown in Video 3 and Figure 6A.

claim: The dissolution of the p-Nephrin/Nck/N-WASP clusters occurs sharply, over a time-span of approximately 2 min, starting approximately 7 min after peptide addition.
source: The dissolution of the clusters occurs sharply, over a time-span of ∼2 min, starting ∼7 min after peptide addition (Figure 6B).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: When TIR is titrated from 100 nM to 100 μM, the fractional intensity of the clusters decreases sharply above 10 μM.
source: When TIR is titrated from 100 nM to 100 μM, the fractional intensity of the clusters also decreases sharply above 10 μM (Figure 6C).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The disassembly of the p-Nephrin/Nck/N-WASP clusters is cooperative.
source: These data suggest that the disassembly of the clusters (similar to the formation) is also cooperative.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data on cluster disassembly.

claim: The p-Nephrin/Nck/N-WASP clusters can effectively promote actin filament assembly through the Arp2/3 complex.
source: These data demonstrate the p-Nephrin/Nck/N-WASP clusters can effectively promote actin filament assembly through the Arp2/3 complex (which is presumably recruited to the membrane through binding N-WASP).
evidence: This is a conclusion from the actin assembly experiments.

claim: Immediately after addition of actin to p-Nephrin/Nck/N-WASP clusters, a small amount of actin, likely monomers, is recruited to the clusters in a relatively uniform fashion.
source: Immediately after addition a small amount of actin, likely monomers, is recruited to the clusters in a relatively uniform fashion (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A.

claim: After a lag of approximately 6–15 min, actin filaments assemble on the p-Nephrin/Nck/N-WASP clusters over a time course of approximately 100 min.
source: After a lag of ∼6–15 min (see below), actin filaments then assemble on the clusters over a time course of approximately 100 min, as visualized by phalloidin 647 staining (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A.

claim: In the absence of the Arp2/3 complex, actin filaments are formed only sparsely in the field of view.
source: In the absence of the Arp2/3 complex, actin filaments are formed only sparsely in the field of view (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B.

claim: In the presence of the Arp2/3 complex, actin appears on the p-Nephrin/Nck/N-WASP clusters much more rapidly and to a much greater degree.
source: In the presence of the Arp2/3 complex, actin appears on the clusters much more rapidly and to a much greater degree (Figure 7A, Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 7A and Figure 7—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The lag time between the initial weak recruitment of actin and the appearance of robust actin fluorescence varies substantially between clusters.
source: The lag time between the initial weak recruitment of actin and the appearance of robust actin fluorescence (presumably representing filaments) varies substantially between clusters (Figure 7A,B).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 7A,B.

claim: Some p-Nephrin/Nck/N-WASP clusters show increased actin after only 6 min, while others remain devoid of additional actin until 10–15 min into the reaction.
source: Some clusters show increased actin after only 6 min, while others remain devoid of additional actin until 10–15 min into the reaction.
evidence: This is an observation from the actin assembly experiments.

claim: The lag time for actin assembly on p-Nephrin/Nck/N-WASP clusters appears to be stochastic.
source: This behavior appears to be stochastic, and the lag time does not show any obvious correlation with size or density of the Nephrin clusters (Figure 7B).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: The lag time for actin assembly does not show any obvious correlation with size or density of the Nephrin clusters.
source: This behavior appears to be stochastic, and the lag time does not show any obvious correlation with size or density of the Nephrin clusters (Figure 7B).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Once actin filament assembly begins on a p-Nephrin/Nck/N-WASP cluster, actin intensity rapidly increases, typically reaching a plateau in less than 10 min.
source: Regardless of when filament assembly begins on a cluster, once it does begin, actin intensity rapidly increases, typically reaching a plateau in less than 10 min (Figure 7C).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: The rapid increase in actin intensity once assembly begins likely reflects strong positive feedback due to activation of the Arp2/3 complex by actin filaments.
source: This behavior likely reflects strong positive feedback due to activation of the Arp2/3 complex by actin filaments (Machesky et al., 1999).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data, supported by citation to Machesky et al., 1999.

claim: As actin filaments assemble, the morphology of the Nephrin clusters changes dramatically, without appreciable changes on overall intensity.
source: As the reaction proceeds, the morphology of the Nephrin clusters changes dramatically, without appreciable changes on overall intensity (except the slow decrease due to photobleaching).
evidence: This is an observation from the actin assembly experiments.

claim: Actin fluorescence remains coincident with Nephrin throughout the actin assembly process.
source: Actin fluorescence remains coincident with Nephrin throughout this process, indicating that the signaling molecules are reorganized by the assembling filaments.
evidence: This is an observation from the actin assembly experiments.

claim: The signaling molecules in p-Nephrin/Nck/N-WASP clusters are reorganized by the assembling actin filaments.
source: Actin fluorescence remains coincident with Nephrin throughout this process, indicating that the signaling molecules are reorganized by the assembling filaments.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the observation that actin and Nephrin remain colocalized.

claim: Shortly after the appearance of actin on a p-Nephrin/Nck/N-WASP cluster, the structure changes from having relatively rounded edges to having many thin hair-like projections from its periphery.
source: Shortly after the appearance of actin on a cluster, the structure changes from having relatively rounded edges to having many thin hair-like projections from its periphery.
evidence: This is an observation from the actin assembly experiments.

claim: The hair-like projections from p-Nephrin/Nck/N-WASP clusters coalesce over time to give the puncta star-like morphologies.
source: These projections coalesce over time to give the puncta star-like morphologies.
evidence: This is an observation from the actin assembly experiments.

claim: Between 42 and 45 min after actin addition, there is a dramatic change in cluster morphology, such that the puncta appear to shatter into a large number of short linear structures.
source: For reasons we cannot currently explain, between 42 and 45 min, well after all of the clusters have recruited significant actin, there is a dramatic change in cluster morphology, such that the puncta appear to shatter into a large number of short linear structures (Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2.

claim: The change in Nephrin morphology between 42 and 45 min coincides with a sharp increase in the total actin localized to the TIRF field/membrane but no change in total Nephrin fluorescence.
source: This change in Nephrin morphology coincides with a sharp increase in the total actin localized to the TIRF field/membrane but no change in total Nephrin fluorescence.
evidence: This is an observation from the actin assembly experiments.

claim: As actin filaments assemble, they cause substantial changes in the morphology of the p-Nephrin/Nck/N-WASP clusters.
source: As the filaments assemble, they cause substantial changes in the morphology of the clusters.
evidence: This is a summary of observations from the actin assembly experiments.

claim: Feedback between actin and the signaling proteins that promote its assembly can control the micron-scale morphology of the entire pathway.
source: This feedback between actin and the signaling proteins that promote its assembly can control the micron-scale morphology of the entire pathway.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the actin assembly data.

claim: Polymerization and concomitant phase separation may contribute generally to the organization of signaling receptors.
source: This process may contribute generally to the organization of signaling receptors.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the findings of the study.

claim: The cytoplasmic tails of many receptors are rapidly phosphorylated on multiple tyrosine residues upon stimulation by extracellular ligands.
source: The cytoplasmic tails of many receptors are rapidly phosphorylated on multiple tyrosine residues upon stimulation by extracellular ligands (Roche et al., 1996; Hunter, 2000; Palmer et al., 2002; Schlessinger, 2000; Houtman et al., 2006; Kaushansky et al., 2008; Wagner et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: Phosphorylation of receptor cytoplasmic tails often occurs concomitant with concentration of the receptors into micron-sized puncta.
source: This often occurs concomitant with concentration of the receptors into micron-sized puncta (Douglass and Vale, 2005; Salaita et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citations to Douglass and Vale, 2005; Salaita et al., 2010.

claim: Receptor puncta persist over many minutes, but exchange molecules in seconds with the surroundings.
source: Where examined, these puncta persist over many minutes, but exchange molecules in seconds with the surroundings, similar to the p-Nephrin/Nck/N-WASP puncta we have generated here.
evidence: This is a comparison between the current study and observations in other systems.

claim: Many receptors use pTyr modifications to engage signaling networks composed of proteins with multiple modular binding domains.
source: Further, many of these receptors have been shown, through combinations of biochemistry and genetics, to use the pTyr modifications to engage signaling networks composed of proteins with multiple modular binding domains, often (but not exclusively) combinations of SH2 domains, SH3 domains, PRMs, and additional pTyr sites.
evidence: This is a statement about general properties of receptor signaling pathways.

claim: T cell activation is controlled by pathways involving multivalent protein interactions.
source: Examples of processes controlled by such pathways include T cell activation (Lee et al., 2003; Dustin et al., 2010)
evidence: Supported by citations to Lee et al., 2003; Dustin et al., 2010.

claim: Invadopodia formation is controlled by pathways involving multivalent protein interactions.
source: invadopodia formation (Oser et al., 2010; Bergman et al., 2014)
evidence: Supported by citations to Oser et al., 2010; Bergman et al., 2014.

claim: Myoblast fusion is controlled by pathways involving multivalent protein interactions.
source: myoblast fusion (Abmayr and Pavlath, 2012)
evidence: Supported by citation to Abmayr and Pavlath, 2012.

claim: Neurite self-avoidance is controlled by pathways involving multivalent protein interactions.
source: neurite self-avoidance (Chen and Maniatis, 2013)
evidence: Supported by citation to Chen and Maniatis, 2013.

claim: Cell–matrix interactions through focal adhesions are controlled by pathways involving multivalent protein interactions.
source: cell–matrix interactions through focal adhesions (Hoffmann et al., 2014)
evidence: Supported by citation to Hoffmann et al., 2014.

claim: Coupled polymerization and phase separation may contribute to the formation of macroscopic puncta in signaling systems composed of multivalent proteins.
source: We hypothesize that coupled polymerization and phase separation may contribute to the formation of macroscopic puncta in these systems and others that are composed similarly.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the findings of the study.

claim: At high densities, a receptor containing a single motif behaves effectively in multivalent fashion and can then cluster through interactions with multivalent ligands.
source: At high densities, a receptor containing a single motif behaves effectively in multivalent fashion and can then cluster through interactions with multivalent ligands.
evidence: This is a statement about the effective valency of receptors at high density.

claim: Proteins with multiple PDZ domains interact with voltage-gated Kv1.4 channels, which are found in clusters at the cell-surface.
source: For example, proteins with multiple PDZ domains interact with voltage-gated Kv1.4 channels, which are found in clusters at the cell-surface (Burke et al., 1999).
evidence: Supported by citation to Burke et al., 1999.

claim: EGF receptors have been reported to form pre-formed oligomers in the absence of ligand.
source: For example, EGF receptors have been reported to form pre-formed oligomers in the absence of ligand (Clayton et al., 2008), effectively increasing the valency of their cytoplasmic tails.
evidence: Supported by citation to Clayton et al., 2008.

claim: Oligomerization of EGF receptors effectively increases the valency of their cytoplasmic tails.
source: For example, EGF receptors have been reported to form pre-formed oligomers in the absence of ligand (Clayton et al., 2008), effectively increasing the valency of their cytoplasmic tails.
evidence: This is an inference from the observation that EGF receptors form oligomers.

claim: Multivalent polymerization and phase separation is particularly prominent in actin regulatory pathways.
source: This behavior appears to be particularly prominent in actin regulatory pathways.
evidence: This is an observation based on the prevalence of multivalent proteins in actin regulatory pathways.

claim: Actin regulatory pathways often contain the adaptor proteins Nck or Crk/CrkL, linked upstream to pTyr-containing proteins and downstream to proline-rich proteins including members of the WASP family.
source: These often contain the adaptor proteins Nck or Crk/CrkL, linked upstream to pTyr-containing proteins and downstream to proline-rich proteins including members of the WASP family (Buday et al., 2002; Antoku et al., 2008; Noy et al., 2012; Chaki and Rivera, 2013; Kaipa et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: Over half of the 29 known ligands of the Nck SH2 domain contain two or more predicted and/or demonstrated Nck binding sites.
source: In this regard, it is notable that over half of the 29 known ligands of the Nck SH2 domain contain two or more (up to 16 in p130 CAS) predicted and/or demonstrated Nck binding sites (Lettau et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to Lettau et al., 2009.

claim: Almost all WASP proteins have large proline-rich regions with multiple SH3-binding PRMs.
source: Further, almost all WASP proteins have large proline-rich regions with multiple SH3-binding PRMs (Padrick and Rosen, 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to Padrick and Rosen, 2010.

claim: WASH is the only WASP protein that does not have a large proline-rich region.
source: The only exception is WASH, which has a small proline-rich region.
evidence: This is a statement about the structure of WASH.

claim: WASH is constitutively associated with the Fam21 protein, which has a large disordered tail that contains 21 LFa peptide motifs that can bind the membrane-associated retromer complex.
source: However, WASH is constitutively associated with the Fam21 protein, which has a large disordered tail that contains 21 so-called LFa peptide motifs that can bind the membrane-associated retromer complex (Derivery et al., 2009; Gomez and Billadeau, 2009; Jia et al., 2010, 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: WASH may have a conceptually similar but molecularly distinct mechanism of assembling into large structures compared to other WASP proteins.
source: Thus WASH may have a conceptually similar but molecularly distinct mechanism of assembling into large structures.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the structure of WASH and its association with Fam21.

claim: The general behavior of multivalent proteins in actin regulatory pathways suggests that clustering may play an important role in spatial and temporal control of actin dynamics.
source: This general behavior suggests that clustering may play an important role in spatial and temporal control of actin dynamics.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the prevalence of multivalent proteins in actin regulatory pathways.

claim: The rate of actin-based motility of N-WASP-coated beads increases non-linearly with increasing WASP density.
source: Pantaloni and colleagues have shown that the rate of actin-based motility of N-WASP-coated beads increases non-linearly with increasing WASP density (Wiesner et al., 2003).
evidence: Supported by citation to Wiesner et al., 2003.

claim: Actin assembly activity scales with the square of N-WASP density at the plasma membrane.
source: Similarly, Ditlev et al. have shown through modeling and cell-based experiments that actin assembly activity scales with the square of N-WASP density at the plasma membrane (Ditlev et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to Ditlev et al., 2012.

claim: A natural consequence of the 2:1 stoichiometry of the WASP:Arp2/3 complex during filament nucleation is that actin assembly activity should increase with the size of WASP clusters.
source: Finally, Padrick et al. showed that a natural consequence of the 2:1 stoichiometry of the WASP:Arp2/3 complex during filament nucleation is that actin assembly activity should increase with the size of WASP clusters and thus the density of WASP at membranes (Padrick et al., 2008).
evidence: Supported by citation to Padrick et al., 2008.

claim: Clustering of receptors and their proximal adaptors may provide a mechanism of concentrating WASP proteins into high-density puncta and thus increasing their activation of the Arp2/3 complex.
source: These observations, together with our data here, suggest that clustering of receptors and their proximal adaptors may provide a mechanism of concentrating WASP proteins into high-density puncta and thus increasing their activation of the Arp2/3 complex, providing local bursts of actin filament assembly.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the findings of the study and previous work.

claim: The mechanism of clustering through multivalent phase separation is not exclusive of, and is expected to act cooperatively with, many other mechanisms that have been proposed to explain receptor clustering.
source: The mechanism we have described is not exclusive of, and in fact is expected to act cooperatively with, many other mechanisms that have been proposed to explain receptor clustering.
evidence: This is a statement about the relationship between the proposed mechanism and other mechanisms.

claim: Interactions between extracellular domains will be thermodynamically coupled to assembly of intracellular oligomers/polymers.
source: Interactions between extracellular domains, as proposed for cadherins and Eph receptors (Himanen et al., 2007; Wu et al., 2011; Seiradake et al., 2013), will be thermodynamically coupled to assembly of intracellular oligomers/polymers.
evidence: This is a statement about thermodynamic coupling between extracellular and intracellular interactions.

claim: Interactions of receptor transmembrane regions with specific lipids should be thermodynamically coupled to the clustering of receptor cytoplasmic tails.
source: Similarly, interactions of receptor transmembrane regions with specific lipids, which can promote concentration of receptors into nano-domains enriched in those lipids, should also be thermodynamically coupled to the clustering of receptor cytoplasmic tails (Lingwood and Simons, 2010).
evidence: This is a statement about thermodynamic coupling between lipid interactions and cytoplasmic tail clustering, supported by citation to Lingwood and Simons, 2010.

claim: ATP-dependent clustering of the cortical acto-myosin system could promote assembly of a phase separated multivalent network if any components of that network can bind to the cytoskeleton.
source: Further, ATP-dependent clustering of the cortical acto-myosin system, which promotes oligomerization of GPI-anchored proteins (Sharma et al., 2004; Goswami et al., 2008), could also promote assembly of a phase separated multivalent network if any components of that network can bind to the cytoskeleton.
evidence: This is a speculation about how acto-myosin clustering could promote phase separation, supported by citations to Sharma et al., 2004; Goswami et al., 2008.

claim: The dynamic rearrangements of the acto-myosin system could control the properties of the signaling clusters and maintain them away from equilibrium.
source: In this case, the dynamic rearrangements of the acto-myosin system could also control the properties of the signaling clusters (e.g., cluster size and/or lifetime of clusters) and maintain them away from equilibrium.
evidence: This is a speculation about how the acto-myosin system could control cluster properties.

source: It is important to note that while weak interactions between extracellular domains or between transmembrane regions and lipids or between receptors and the cytoskeleton may not on their own produce significant oligomerization of receptors, these energies could have substantial effects when combined with energies of clustering.
evidence: This is a statement about the potential additive effects of different types of interactions.

claim: Weak interactions could have strong effects on the critical concentrations or the degree of receptor phosphorylation needed for phase separation/clustering through adaptor-based intracellular interactions.
source: Phrased differently, these other interactions could have strong effects on the critical concentrations (or the degree of receptor phosphorylation) needed for phase separation/clustering through adaptor-based intracellular interactions.
evidence: This is a statement about how weak interactions could affect clustering parameters.

claim: The ability of membrane receptors to cluster through multivalent phase separation could generate a sharp switch between different states.
source: The ability of membrane receptors to cluster through multivalent phase separation could have a number of functional implications in cells. The process will generate a sharp switch between different states, which will depend on the concentrations of at least two (and possibly several) species, as well as the degree of receptor phosphorylation in pTyr-dependent cases.
evidence: This is a speculation about functional implications of clustering.

claim: The switch to clustering could be tightly controlled, either through relatively slow changes in protein concentration or more rapidly through changes in receptor phosphorylation or oligomerization by extracellular ligands.
source: Thus, the switch could be tightly controlled, either through relatively slow changes in protein concentration or more rapidly through changes in receptor phosphorylation or oligomerization by extracellular ligands.
evidence: This is a speculation about how clustering could be controlled.

claim: The phase-separated state will have different density, composition, and dynamics from the surrounding regions of the membrane, each of which could have functional consequences.
source: The phase-separated state will have different density, composition, and dynamics from the surrounding regions of the membrane, each of which could have functional consequences.
evidence: This is a statement about the properties of phase-separated regions.

claim: Increasing density of WASP proteins leads to non-linear increases in actin assembly activity.
source: In the case of actin regulatory systems, we and others have shown that because WASP proteins bind (and activate) Arp2/3 complex in 2:1 fashion, increasing density of WASP proteins leads to non-linear increases in actin assembly activity (Padrick et al., 2008; Ditlev et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to Padrick et al., 2008; Ditlev et al., 2012.

claim: Clustering should provide not only spatial organization of the actin filament network but also increased biochemical signaling activity.
source: Thus, clustering should provide not only spatial organization of the actin filament network (decreasing spatial noise [Grecco et al., 2011]) but also increased biochemical signaling activity.
evidence: This is a speculation about the functional consequences of clustering, with citation to Grecco et al., 2011.

claim: The enhancement due to clustering would be particularly strong for systems with positive feedback, as in Arp2/3 complex–actin pathways.
source: The enhancement due to clustering would be particularly strong for systems with positive feedback, as in Arp2/3 complex–actin pathways.
evidence: This is a speculation about the effect of positive feedback on clustering.

claim: Other proteins and lipids could be concentrated into or excluded from the phase-separated structure.
source: In addition to the polymer components themselves, other proteins and lipids could be concentrated into or excluded from the phase-separated structure.
evidence: This is a speculation about partitioning of molecules into phase-separated structures.

claim: Partitioning of molecules into phase-separated structures could be dictated by both specific interactions and non-specific electrostatic and/or hydrophobic interactions with the polymer matrix.
source: This partitioning could be dictated by both specific interactions (e.g., a monovalent SH3 protein could be recruited to the p-Nephrin/Nck/N-WASP clusters by binding the PRMs of N-WASP) as well as non-specific electrostatic and/or hydrophobic interactions with the polymer matrix.
evidence: This is a speculation about mechanisms of partitioning.

claim: The collection of molecules in phase-separated structures would produce a distinct biochemical environment from the surrounding regions.
source: The collection of these molecules would then produce a distinct biochemical environment from the surrounding regions, favoring or disfavoring certain reactions or afford specificity to signaling pathways.
evidence: This is a speculation about the functional consequences of partitioning.

claim: Phase-separated clusters could potentially act as sites of enzymatic modification and release.
source: Since the clusters are temporally stable but readily exchange molecules with the surroundings, they could potentially act as sites of enzymatic modification and release.
evidence: This is a speculation about a potential function of clusters.

source: Finally, the structural and dynamic features of the polymer matrix could also influence the rates and/or specificities of reactions that occur within the clusters.
evidence: This is a speculation about how the polymer matrix could affect reactions.

claim: Nephrin is constitutively phosphorylated in the slit diaphragm between podocytes of the kidney.
source: Recent data have shown that Nephrin is constitutively phosphorylated in the slit diaphragm between podocytes of the kidney (Jones et al., 2009; New et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to Jones et al., 2009; New et al., 2013.

claim: The loss of Nck disrupts the filtration capacity of the slit diaphragm, concomitant with the loss of cortical actin filaments.
source: Previous data showed that the loss of Nck disrupts the filtration capacity of the diaphragm, concomitant with the loss of cortical actin filaments (Jones et al., 2006).

claim: The pathway from p-Nephrin to actin, and by inference the polymeric network described in this study, is important in maintaining the slit diaphragm.
source: These observations suggest that the pathway from p-Nephrin to actin, and by inference the polymeric network we have described here, is important in maintaining the slit diaphragm.
evidence: This is an inference from the observations about Nephrin phosphorylation and Nck function.

claim: The extracellular portion of Nephrin is composed of multiple IgG domains and FNIII domains.
source: The extracellular portion of Nephrin is composed of multiple IgG domains and FNIII domains.
evidence: This is a statement about the structure of Nephrin.

claim: The extracellular domains of Nephrin have been suggested to self-associate, both in trans across the slit diaphragm and in cis within individual cells.
source: These have been suggested to self-associate, both in trans across the slit diaphragm and in cis within individual cells (Gerke et al., 2003).
evidence: Supported by citation to Gerke et al., 2003.

claim: Self-association of Nephrin extracellular domains in cis should promote polymerization and phase separation of the actin pathway components.
source: The latter should promote polymerization and phase separation of the actin pathway components.
evidence: This is an inference from the observation that Nephrin extracellular domains can self-associate in cis.

claim: The Nephrin system may be a case where interactions on both sides of the plasma membrane act cooperatively to produce a polymeric structure with both extracellular functions and intracellular functions.
source: Thus, this system may be a case where interactions on both sides of the plasma membrane act cooperatively to produce a polymeric structure with both extracellular functions (the filtration barrier) and intracellular functions (signaling to actin).
evidence: This is a speculation about the cooperative nature of extracellular and intracellular interactions in the Nephrin system.

claim: Interactions between multivalent proteins at membranes can lead to concomitant polymerization and phase separation, generating micron-size clusters.
source: In summary, we have shown that interactions between multivalent proteins at membranes can lead to concomitant polymerization and phase separation, generating micron-size clusters.
evidence: This is a summary of the main finding of the study.

claim: The analogous construction of many signaling pathways suggests that the behavior of multivalent phase separation could be quite general.
source: Although only demonstrated here for the p-Nephrin/Nck/N-WASP system, the analogous construction of many signaling pathways suggests that this behavior could be quite general, and relevant to many biological processes.
evidence: This is a speculation about the generality of the findings.

claim: Polymerization and phase separation at membranes could impart spatial organization on signaling pathways and afford them strongly non-linear activities.
source: Polymerization and phase separation at membranes could impart spatial organization on these pathways and afford them strongly non-linear activities.
evidence: This is a speculation about the functional consequences of phase separation.
